The core of GraphQL's operational logic lies in its ability to parse and validate requests before execution. The parser (primitive 1) extracts structured data from raw HTTP payloads, converting them into abstract syntax trees that represent queries, mutations, or subscriptions. This process ensures syntactic correctness and enables downstream processing. The validator (primitive 2) then checks that all variables are properly formatted as objects, preventing runtime errors due to malformed input. Finally, the execution context builder (primitive 3) ties together these components with a schema to create a runtime environment for resolving fields. These primitives form a closed-loop system where each step depends on the previous one, ensuring that only well-formed operations proceed to execution. Failure at any stage results in immediate rejection, maintaining system integrity. The dual nature of this architecture—syntax parsing followed by semantic validation—mirrors the duality seen in physical systems where structure determines behavior. Each primitive operates within a specific regime defined by its assumptions and breakdown conditions, creating a robust foundation for distributed query resolution.
